perspective:
Harold’s accessible information:

- He knows he is a project manager leading a project. He believes his team is underperforming because they lack motivation, and he feels frustrated and anxious about it.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer and trusted friend/advisor he turns to for support.
- He arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur. He told Arthur that his project team seems unmotivated and that it is affecting progress.
- He heard Arthur advise him to understand what drives each team member individually, have one-on-one conversations, and make people feel valued and understood.
- After that conversation, Harold felt hopeful and relieved. He decided to try Arthur’s advice.
- In a team meeting, Harold proposed quick one-on-one chats to understand each person’s motivation. He heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each of them.
- Later, Harold observed that the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- He told Arthur this. He heard Arthur suggest there may be deeper or underlying team issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold decided to set up another round of meetings.
- In one-on-one meetings, Harold asked team members to share concerns or problems. He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few team members affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold told them he would look into resolving conflicts, redistribute tasks to ease pressure, and that their well-being mattered.
- He then felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve team performance.
- He told the team he would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- He heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help them work better together. He heard Team Member 2 agree and say it was good that concerns were being addressed.
- Harold told the team their input and well-being were crucial and that they should work together to make the project a success.

He does not have access to anything Arthur or the team members did not say or show him, nor to narrator-only or private information beyond these interactions and his prior friendship/advice relationship with Arthur.
